headline: 30 trades, net -1.04 bps/bet (total -31.3); rolling 17-bet gross slipped to -2.39 bps. Signal flat at 0.
regime_note: BTC ~$83.9k, still consolidating well above the mid-August low-$60ks after the late-August step-up; choppy, high-variance tape. Signal is 0, so no live position right now.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing.** Across all 30 resolved live trades the strategy is net **-1.04 bps/bet** (total **-31.3 bps**), with a 40% win rate. The most recent rolling window of 17 bets is **-5.39 bps net** / **-2.39 bps gross** at an assumed 3 bps cost. Signal is currently 0, so nothing is open.

**What changed vs last time.** Barely anything. Trade count ticked from 30 toward a fuller ledger, and the rolling gross drifted from roughly flat (~-0.97 bps) to -2.39 bps. That's a small, noise-sized move, not a new trend.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us.** Remember the backtested edge was only ~4 bps gross against a ~3.9 bps breakeven — marginal by design. The live trades are wildly dispersed: individual results run from **+48.7 bps** to **-28.1 bps**. With only 17-30 bets, a couple of big losers (e.g. the -28 and -13 bps prints) dominate the average. A sample this small cannot distinguish 'the edge is gone' from 'ordinary bad luck.' It simply is not enough data to judge.

**Bottom line.** Live results are mildly negative and gross is now slightly below zero, which is worth watching but fully consistent with a thin, high-variance sample of a strategy that was never expected to clear costs reliably. No action warranted yet. Also note: the independent edge search still has **0 survivors** at the 5 bps bar — a reminder this was always marginal, not a money printer. No profit is implied or guaranteed.
